answer: Bind each agent to a physical board and fingerprint its quartz oscillator by its manufacturing-unique clock drift. Periodically every identity must timestamp a random beacon drawn from an ocean of unpredictable samples; the server recomputes the drift curve and rejects any whose signature fails to match its enrolled one, so replays and shared devices collapse to one curve. Solder joints are imaged too: aged boards show an umber oxidation tint a freshly spun clone lacks. A 10,000-identity farm thus needs 10,000 real aged boards at about 40 dollars each.
